dedupe_keys.name: tehran window dimension energy and comfort simulations

description: Seyed Mohammad Reza Adel Nasab publishes this synthetic window-geometry dataset on Zenodo for a Tehran building energy and thermal-comfort study. Its documentation says each CSV row represents a window-width and window-height configuration simulated with Rhino, Grasshopper, Honeybee and EnergyPlus. Documented outputs are annual cooling and heating demand in kWh and the percentage of occupied hours within an ASHRAE 55 adaptive comfort range. Zenodo metadata lists dataset.csv, code.py, a Grasshopper script and a short readme, under CC BY 4.0 with open access. The readme also names data/data2_cleaned.csv, code/run_all.py and requirements.txt, which do not match the current Zenodo file manifest. This mismatch leaves exact reproduction steps uncertain; no CSV rows or code were downloaded or run. Simulation use includes testing a surrogate for window-design optimisation in a hot-dry climate, subject to the original room and weather assumptions. It complements model-energyplus as a small published output set from an EnergyPlus workflow, not as measured building performance. A caveat is that one Tehran scenario cannot establish performance for other building types or climates.
